title: Search-on-Graph: Iterative Informed Navigation for Large Language Model Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Knowledge-intensive reasoning with LLMs and knowledge graphs requires selecting appropriate reasoning paths.

gap.claim: Existing path-selection methods often use separate modules with criteria weakly connected to reasoning requirements, causing incorrect relation selection or premature pruning of relevant paths.

contributions.claim: Search-on-Graph connects path selection to reasoning by having the LLM select relations using the available knowledge-graph structure and complete reasoning history.
SoG implements an observe-think-navigate process in which the LLM evaluates available relations, reasons about the most useful path, and navigates at each step.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On six KGQA benchmarks, the authors report that SoG outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that SoG requires no task-specific fine-tuning and generalizes across different knowledge-graph schemas.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs augmented with knowledge graphs are presented as a promising approach for knowledge-intensive reasoning.
Selecting appropriate reasoning paths is central to the approach.
Separate path-selection modules use weakly connected criteria and may select incorrect relations or prune relevant paths too early.
SoG uses the LLM's reasoning history and knowledge-graph structure to select relations through observe-think-navigate steps.
Experiments on six KGQA benchmarks report improvements over state-of-the-art methods, without task-specific fine-tuning and across different schemas.

source_observation.claim: The method makes path selection part of the LLM's ongoing reasoning process and conditions navigation on the full reasoning history.

interpretation.claim: Coupling search decisions with task reasoning may reduce errors caused by selection criteria that are disconnected from the current reasoning objective.

application.claim: For iterative graph-based reasoning systems, consider selecting the next relation using both local graph structure and accumulated reasoning context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy improves performance outside the reported KGQA benchmarks or under different resource constraints.

unknowns: Benchmark names, datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not reported.
The abstract does not specify the implementation details, computational cost, or failure cases of SoG.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
